extracted.intended_audience: poets, poetry critics, and literary friends (Romantic-era poets)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative comments on composing and judging poems (lyric, pastoral, dramatic pieces), covering imagery, metre, voice, originality, tone, and editorial decisions. Framed as letters between poets giving concrete praise and criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of incident and characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid trite or overused catastrophes/plots (e.g., 'Joanna's ruin is a catastrophe too trite').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary circumstances in the conclusion; consider novel character-types (e.g., a rustic country fellow instead of the familiar gentleman seducer — a 'Roger-Lothario' would be a novel character). The example shows that changing the agent of a familiar plot can refresh it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture-work and circumstantial detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Full of picture-work and circumstances pleases the reader ('it pleases me mightily, being so full of picture-work and circumstances').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rich scene-painting and concrete particulars enhance a poem's appeal; selecting picturesque moments aids effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Felicity of phrase / careful word-choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain lines or stanzas can 'have no felicity of phrase' and thus fall off in quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid epithets or single words that 'dash' the poem (example: an ill-chosen epithet like 'enviable' can ruin a fine stanza). Choose words that fit tone and feeling precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure, metre, and novel rhythmic choice
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'measure, too, is novel and pleasing' can be a strong asset; be attentive to metrical novelty and suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New or pleasing measures may distinguish a poem; but be wary of strict/formal pedantry — naturalness of meter often matters more than slavish adherence to rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid slavish formalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of poets who insist on mechanical rules (e.g., 'could not comprehend how that could be poetry which did not go upon ten feet').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not elevate technical constraints (like fixed line-length) above expressive needs; resist prescriptive dogmatism about form when it hinders feeling or effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness of rhyme and concealment of art
rubrics_metrics.description: Disliked are rhymes made ostentatious (e.g., rhymes that 'keep a comfortable distance of six or eight lines apart' and are pointed out before recitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rhyme should feel organic, not announced or made into a parlor trick; avoid contrivances that call attention to themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional hold / pathos
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry that 'lays hold of the heart' or produces deep pathos (e.g., 'A spring of love gush'd from my heart') is highly valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek passages that genuinely move the reader; select examples of a poem that show its power to stir emotion rather than focusing only on cleverness or novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend of ludicrous and terrible (comic/terrible mixture)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mixture of the ludicrous and the terrible can be effective (Marlowe lines described as 'mixture of the ludicrous and the terrible').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juxtaposing grotesque/terrible material with comic elements can produce striking effects when handled with genius; this is given as praise for certain dramatic passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice consistency and character-appropriate imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagery and strange conceits should suit the speaker ('Witches illustrate, as fine ladies do, from their own familiar objects').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strangeness in image is acceptable when it fits the character's perspective or voice; character-driven metaphors enhance verisimilitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terseness and jocular pathos
rubrics_metrics.description: A terseness combined with 'jocular pathos' can make one 'feel in laughter' and be especially effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economy of expression and a blend of humor with tenderness often produce strong reader response; avoid verbosity that blunts emotional effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility / familiar tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Some writing 'comes tenfold better recommended to the heart, comes there more like a neighbor or familiar' than more ornate or sentimental verse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An accessible, intimate tone often connects more powerfully with readers than high-flown sentimentality; consider familiar phrasing and domestic touches to engage the heart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter invention (rescuing humble subjects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening an 'intercourse' with despised animals/insects — poems addressed to rats, toads, worms, etc. — is proposed as novel and morally useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploring neglected or contemptible subjects can renew poetic possibilities and produce moral and pleasurable results; novel subjects are recommended as a series (with illustrative plates suggested).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial boldness in revision
rubrics_metrics.description: When editing, 'cut deeper' — be willing to pare work ('I perfectly accede to all your alterations, and only desire that you had cut deeper').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be decisive in revision; greater cuts often improve clarity and effect. Encourages courage in excision during editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative selection when reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: A reviewer should not cherry-pick odd passages while ignoring fifty equally miraculous ones ('You have selected a passage fertile in unmeaning miracles, but have passed by fifty passages as miraculous as the miracles they celebrate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When critiquing, choose representative examples and acknowledge a work's range rather than construing isolated lines to support a narrow verdict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone-appropriate praise; beware flattering epithets
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful about labeling people with flattering epithets that misrepresent ('don't make me ridiculous any more by terming me gentle-hearted... the meaning of "gentle" is equivocal').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise should be sincere and precise; avoid labels or compliments that distort the subject's character or reduce them to an awkward trope.
